summary:
The Porbeagle was a powerful, cold-water shark — muscular and built for speed — roaming the temperate and sub-Antarctic waters of the North Atlantic and Southern Hemisphere. Capable of reaching nearly twelve feet in length, it pursued fish through some of the ocean's most remote and frigid depths, living up to sixty years in southern waters.

Its downfall came quietly, through nets and longlines — targeted for its meat and fins, caught incidentally by industrial fleets across open seas. With small litters and slow maturity, the Porbeagle could not replenish itself fast enough to survive commercial pressure. Its populations continue to decline, a reminder of how swiftly we can diminish what the ocean took millennia to shape.
